title: Net primary productivity
back: Only NPP is available to herbivores and decomposers. Units g m⁻² yr⁻¹ or kcal m⁻² yr⁻¹.

title: Biosphere productivity
back: Oceans cover 70% of Earth but make only about a third of NPP.

title: Decomposition
back: First three act on detritus together; humification and mineralisation in soil. Humus is a slow, colloidal nutrient reservoir.

title: Decomposition rate
tex: \begin{gathered}\text{N, sugars, warm, moist}\\\text{lignin, chitin, cold, anaerobic}\end{gathered}
back: Temperature and soil moisture are the most important climatic factors.

title: Capturing sunlight
back: Energy flow is unidirectional: Sun → producers → consumers. Deep-sea hydrothermal vents are the exception.

title: GFC vs DFC
back: GFC is the main energy route in water; on land more energy flows through the DFC.

title: 10 per cent law
legend: E_n = energy at trophic level n
back: 10,000 J → 1,000 → 100 → 10 J at the tertiary consumer.

title: Energy and biomass pyramids
back: Energy pyramid always upright. Biomass in the sea is inverted: fast-dividing phytoplankton support more fish biomass.

title: Limits of ecological pyramids
tex: \begin{gathered}\text{one species, two levels}\\\text{no food webs}\\\text{no saprophytes}\end{gathered}
back: Pyramids assume a simple food chain, which almost never exists in nature.

title: Which pyramid never flips
back: Biomass flips in the Blue sea; Numbers flip on a (Neem) tree; Energy never, because heat is lost at every step.
